answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and publishes one key-signed ferrous alloy recipe on the lantern board, with its mix and schedule. A falcon auditor reproduces it in the lab and reports; a mismatch or duplicate recipe hash burns the bond. The first lab fee is 25 credits, and the kth fake pays 25+4(k-1), so the 1000th pays 4021; 1000 fakes pay 2,023,000 in fees, locking 70,000 in bonds. A rented-recipe ring fails because signature and sample must match the identity key, and a reused hash burns both bonds. An honest agent pays 25 once and recovers the bond after a clean audit.
